newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil deputies approve bill to curb gun use.
newsitem.headline: Brazil deputies approve bill to curb gun use.

text.p: Brazil's Chamber of Deputies approved a bill on Wednesday that seeks to curb gun use and reduce the country's high levels of violence.

The bill introduces stiff new jail sentences for unauthorised carrying of guns. It was presented to Congress in 1996 but ran into entrenched opposition from lawmakers unwilling to restrict Brazil's traditional lax rules on carrying firearms.
Last year, President Fernando Henrique Cardoso urged Congress to approve the legislation which has been approved in the Senate and he is due to sign into law on Thursday.

"Up to now, a crook caught with an AR-15 (assault rifle) faced between 15 days and six months in jail. Now he'll be looking at at least two years and a maximum of six," said deputy Roberto Jefferson who drew up the legislation.
The law requires owners of firearms to register their weapons with a new National Arms System within six months.

After that, people caught with unauthorised handguns of up to .38 calibre, or replicas of weapons, face between one and two years in jail. Unlicensed bigger guns carry sentences of up to four years, with an extra two years possible for owners of smuggled weapons.

Jefferson said the new law would make it easier for police to put members of armed gangs behind bars. It would also defuse tensions in Brazil's countryside where armed landowners and landless peasants clash regularly, he said.

Thirty-one of every 100,000 Brazilians are murdered, compared with 20 in Mexico and 10 in the United States. Murder is the leading cause of death for Brazilian men aged 20-29, according to official statistics.
